annotation.title_clean: Draft Memorandum: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications
annotation.title_en: Draft Memorandum: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President
annotation.summary_en: Draft OMB memorandum implementing Executive Order 13859, guiding US federal agencies on regulating private-sector AI applications. It stresses innovation, avoiding precautionary regulation, cost-benefit and risk-based approaches, non-regulatory options and reliance on voluntary standards, and requires agency AI plans. Government use of AI is excluded.
key_provisions_or_claims: Agencies must avoid regulatory or non-regulatory actions that needlessly hamper AI innovation and growth.

Ten principles for stewardship: public trust, participation, scientific integrity, risk assessment, benefits and costs, flexibility, fairness, disclosure, safety and security, interagency coordination.
Agencies should favor non-regulatory approaches such as voluntary consensus standards and private-sector conformity assessment.
Agencies should consider preempting inconsistent state AI laws or forgo regulation where a uniform national standard is unnecessary.
Agencies must submit plans listing statutory authorities, AI use cases, regulatory barriers and planned actions.
